title: SCIM: deprovision handshake & reclaim window with audit trace
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a safe deprovisioning handshake for SCIM that pairs each delete with a causal audit trace and a timeboxed reclaim window accessible from the admin console. This ticket covers protocol changes, worker sequencing, idempotency tokens, exponential-jitter retry policy, and the UI/ops flow to recover accidentally deprovisioned users/groups.
acceptance_criteria: Every SCIM delete is recorded with a causal audit ID that surfaces in logs and the admin console
Deprovision transitions to a soft-deleted 'reclaimable' state for a configurable window (default 72h) before permanent removal
Workers use monotonic operation IDs + idempotency token to prevent duplicate deletes during retries and failover
Retry policy uses exponential backoff with full jitter and capped attempts; failed deletes move to a dead-letter with clear remediation steps
Admin console lists reclaimable subjects with audit trail link and a one-click restore that is safe to run concurrently
E2E tests and chaos tests prove no accidental permanent deletion during multi-region failover
design_decisions: Introduce 'reclaim_window' state on User/Group records instead of immediate tombstone to allow admin recovery
Attach a 'causal_audit_id' (uuid) to every SCIM mutation; propagate to logs, tracing, and console links
Sequence operations using a cluster-wide monotonic op_id generator to ensure deterministic apply order across workers
Idempotency: require SCIM client idempotency_token header; server maps token to op outcomes for dedupe within window
Retry policy: use exponential backoff with full jitter (base=300ms, cap=30s, max_attempts=8) and escalate to DLQ after backoff exhaustion
Expose a compact restore API used by the console that validates atomic preconditions (no re-created conflicting identity)
implementation_notes: Schema: add fields 'deprovisioned_at', 'reclaim_until', 'reclaim_state', 'causal_audit_id' to identity table
Runtime: worker will check op_id ordering and consult idempotency map before applying delete; write-ahead record created for audit
DLQ: create 'scim_deletes_dlq' Kafka topic with schema (causal_audit_id, payload, last_error, attempts, last_attempt_at)
Permissions: only admins with 'reclaim:restore' scope can perform manual restore in console
Migration: backfill reclaim_until = deprovisioned_at + default_window for existing soft-deleted records; script must be idempotent
test_plan: Unit tests for idempotency map, op_id sequencing, and reclaim state transitions
Integration test: SCIM provisioning -> delete -> console restore within window -> verify re-linked resources
Chaos test: kill primary worker during mid-delete and assert no double-delete and that DLQ receives failed payload
Load test: simulate burst deletes to validate backoff and DLQ behavior under pressure
Security test: RBAC assertions to ensure only allowed roles can restore
E2E QA checklist with customer-simulated SCIM directory (Okta/G-suite)
rollout_plan: Stage 1: internal tenants only, monitor metrics and SLOs for 72h
Stage 2: invite pilot customers (opt-in), collect feedback and audit traces
Stage 3: gradual ramp to all tenants, enable migration backfill in small batches
Fallback: flag off will revert to previous immediate-deletion behavior; DLQ processing paused
Incident runbook: steps to manually restore from DLQ and to rollback schema changes if needed
